proofs.title: 27 qubits cannot be order-7 AC
proofs.summary: A rigorously validated four-copy positivity certificate excludes every pure order-7 AC state.
proofs.bodyHtml:
A hypothetical state gives a positive, trace-one rotationally averaged tensor-power moment. Vanishing spin multipoles through the specified order impose linear first-leg contraction equations.

Exact factorial Clebsch–Gordan contractions and outward-rounded interval arithmetic certify a strictly positive separating combination. Recursive projection and polar-normalization bounds validate the complete symmetric representation. This contradicts trace one for arbitrary complex symmetric states.

The currently proved interval for the maximum order is 5–6; failure to find an intermediate-order state is not used as an exclusion proof.

proofs.title: 28 qubits: maximum pure AC order is 6
proofs.summary: A rigorously validated four-copy positivity certificate excludes every pure order-7 AC state.

proofs.title: 28 qubits cannot be order-8 AC
proofs.summary: An exact rational three-copy positivity certificate excludes every pure order-8 AC state.
proofs.bodyHtml:
A hypothetical state gives a positive, trace-one rotationally averaged tensor-power moment. Vanishing spin multipoles through the specified order impose linear first-leg contraction equations.

An exact rational identity expresses the negative trace as a sum of those vanishing equations and nonnegative matrix traces. The independent standard-library verifier reconstructs all physical contraction rows, trace factors, and positive matrices. The contradiction covers arbitrary complex symmetric states.

This is an auxiliary certificate. The stronger seventh-order exclusion proves that the maximum pure AC order at 28 qubits is six.
